title: Zero-Cost Git-Native Publishing: Decoupled CMS Without Server Lock-In
author: Subimpact Engineering
excerpt: How Kaze decouples the editorial studio from the static generator, allowing teams to use Sveltia CMS, Obsidian, or VS Code interchangeably.
body:
Static site generators often struggle with non-technical content editing. The industry usually solves this by pushing teams toward proprietary SaaS headless CMS providers with hefty monthly subscription fees and database lock-in.

### Complete Separation of Concerns

Kaze solves this through strict decoupling:

1. **The Generator is CMS-Agnostic:** Kaze only reads plain JSON and Markdown files from the `content/` folder. It has zero knowledge of how those files were created or edited.
2. **Open Standards:** The optional `/admin/` visual studio uses the open Decap/Sveltia specification. Any tool that adheres to this standard works out of the box.
3. **Zero Running Costs:** Sveltia CMS runs entirely in the client browser as a single-page application. It commits changes directly to your Git repository, triggering automatic edge deployments with $0 server fees.

### Workflows for Every Role

- **Developers:** Edit content locally in Neovim, VS Code, or Cursor. Push commits via Git CLI.
- **Writers and Editors:** Log into `/admin/` through GitHub authentication to edit articles, upload photos, and draft case studies with a visual interface.
- **Knowledge Workers:** Point an Obsidian vault directly at `content/` to sync notes into live web pages.

Because the underlying data is standard JSON and Markdown, you retain full ownership of your content forever.

faq.q: Can I remove Sveltia CMS if I do not need it?
faq.a: Yes. Deleting the entire admin directory has zero impact on Kaze. The build script does not depend on Sveltia.

faq.q: What happens when an editor saves changes in the CMS?
faq.a: The CMS creates a git commit directly to your GitHub repository. Your hosting platform (such as Cloudflare Pages) detects the commit and rebuilds the static files automatically.
